description: Modern C++ from the first program to classes, templates and the standard library, with attention to the memory model that makes C++ both fast and dangerous. Taught to the depth of a leading programming abstractions course in C++.
modelledOn: Stroustrup, Programming: Principles and Practice Using C++
outcomes: Write, compile and run C++ programs that use the standard namespace, I/O streams and clear structure.
Use variables, constants, expressions, statements and all control-flow constructs correctly.
Design functions with value, reference and pointer parameters, overloading and default arguments.
Use arrays, C-strings, std::string and std::vector and explain their memory layout.
Manage memory with pointers, new and delete, and smart pointers, avoiding leaks and dangling pointers.
Design classes with constructors, destructors, encapsulation, operator overloading and inheritance.

units.title: Creating a program
topics: The C++ toolchain: editor, compiler (g++ or clang++), linker, running; compiler flags and warnings
Structure of a program: main, headers, the std namespace, using declarations
Comments and documentation; code style
cout, cin, cerr; iostream manipulators

units.title: Variables and constants
topics: Fundamental types: int, long, char, bool, float, double; sizes and ranges; auto
Declaration, initialisation (including brace initialisation) and assignment
const and constexpr; literals and enumerations; scoped enums
Type conversion: implicit, static_cast; narrowing

units.title: Expressions and statements
topics: Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise and assignment operators; precedence and associativity
Integer division, overflow and floating-point precision
Compound statements, blocks and scope; lvalues and rvalues in brief
std::string and basic string operations; stringstream

units.title: Program flow
topics: if, else, switch; the conditional operator
while, do-while, for and range-based for; break and continue
Nested loops and loop invariants; common patterns: counters, accumulators, sentinels
Reading until end of file; input validation and error recovery
Debugging with a debugger and assertions

units.title: Functions
topics: Declaration, definition, prototypes, header and source files, multiple-file programs
Pass by value, by reference, by const reference; return values; inline
Overloading, default arguments, scope and lifetime, static locals
Recursion: factorial, Fibonacci, binary search, permutations, Tower of Hanoi
Function templates; lambda expressions
The call stack and stack overflow

units.title: Arrays
topics: Built-in arrays, initialisation, bounds and undefined behaviour; std::array
Multidimensional arrays; passing arrays to functions
std::vector: push_back, size, iteration, iterators; searching and sorting with <algorithm>
C-strings and char arrays versus std::string
Simple algorithms: linear and binary search, selection and insertion sort

units.title: Pointers
topics: Addresses, pointer declaration, dereferencing, nullptr; pointers and arrays; pointer arithmetic
Dynamic memory: new, delete, new[], delete[]; leaks and dangling pointers
References versus pointers; pointers as function parameters
Linked list and dynamic array built by hand
Smart pointers: unique_ptr and shared_ptr; RAII as the C++ way
Memory errors and tools: AddressSanitizer and Valgrind

units.title: Classes
topics: Class definition, public and private, member functions, this; separating interface and implementation
Constructors, default and parameterised; destructors; initialiser lists; copy constructor and assignment; the rule of three/five
Operator overloading: arithmetic, comparison, stream insertion
Static members, friend functions, const member functions
Inheritance, virtual functions, abstract classes and polymorphism
Class templates and the standard containers (vector, map, set) and iterators
Project: a bank, library or inventory system built from classes with persistent file storage

schedule.title: The toolchain and your first programs
schedule.exercise: Describe in a short paragraph what the preprocessor, compiler and linker each do to a source file before it runs.

tasks.title: Compile and run a hello program with warnings turned on, then introduce a missing semicolon and a missing include and read each error message
Write a program that reads a name and two numbers with cin, prints their sum with cout and uses manipulators to align a three-column table
Split a program into a header and two source files, fix a given set of linker errors and explain the cause of each in comments

schedule.title: Types, initialisation and conversion
schedule.exercise: Predict the output of eight short snippets about integer ranges and conversions, then run them and explain each surprise.

tasks.title: Print the size and range of each fundamental type and show what happens when an int variable exceeds its maximum
Define a scoped enum for days of the week and constexpr constants for tax rates, and use them in a pay calculation
Find five narrowing and implicit conversion bugs in a given program, fix them with brace initialisation and static_cast, and check the outputs

schedule.title: Operators, expressions and strings
schedule.exercise: Evaluate by hand six expressions mixing operators and precedence, then verify each with a program.

tasks.title: Write a program that uses bitwise operators to set, clear and test individual flag bits in an unsigned byte
Show integer division truncation, remainder with negative numbers and floating point rounding with six examples and explain each result
Parse a line of comma separated student records using std::string and stringstream and print a cleaned table, handling blank and malformed fields

schedule.title: Selection and repetition
schedule.exercise: Write pseudocode for a program that finds the largest of a list of numbers ending with a sentinel, then trace it with five values.

tasks.title: Write a switch-based menu that converts between cedis, dollars and pounds, with a default case for invalid choices
Print a triangle of stars and a table of squares using for, while and range-based for loops, and check the line counts
Find all perfect numbers below 10000 with nested loops and prove the loop invariant used, then reduce the run time by tightening the loop bounds

schedule.title: Input handling and debugging
schedule.exercise: Write a bug report for a given failing program describing the symptom, the cause you found and the fix.

tasks.title: Read integers until end of file, skipping bad tokens, and print count and mean, then test with five malformed inputs
Step through a buggy loop with a debugger-style visualiser, watch the variables change and find the off-by-one error
Add assertions and a validated input loop to a grade-processing program, then locate and fix three planted bugs with the debugger

schedule.title: Functions and multiple files
schedule.exercise: Draw the stack frames for a call to a function that takes one parameter by value and another by reference.

tasks.title: Write swap functions that take pointers, values and references, and show which ones change the caller's variables
Create a multiple-file program with a header, an implementation and a main file for a temperature library, and build it without errors
Design an overloaded area function set with default arguments and a static counter of calls, and verify the counter and outputs across 12 calls

schedule.title: Recursion, templates and the call stack
schedule.exercise: Trace the recursive calls of Tower of Hanoi for three disks and list all seven moves.

tasks.title: Step through recursive factorial and Fibonacci in the visualiser and note the call stack depth at the deepest point
Write a function template for maximum and a lambda sort comparator, and use them on integers, doubles and strings
Trigger a stack overflow with runaway recursion, measure the maximum safe depth, and rewrite the function iteratively to remove the limit

schedule.title: Arrays, vectors and simple algorithms
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why reading past the end of an array is undefined behaviour and what symptoms it can produce.

tasks.title: Fill an array of 10 marks, find the average and highest, then deliberately read out of bounds and observe what the std::array version does
Use std::vector and the algorithm library to sort, search and remove duplicates from a list of 20 student numbers
Trace binary search and insertion sort step by step on 10 values, then implement both and compare comparison counts for sorted and reversed input

schedule.title: Pointers and dynamic memory
schedule.exercise: Draw a memory diagram of a pointer to an int and a pointer to an array, showing addresses and the values that dereferencing gives.

tasks.title: Follow a pointer through an array with pointer arithmetic in the visualiser and record the address and value at each step
Allocate and free a dynamic array with new and delete, then write a version with a leak and one with a dangling pointer and explain each
Rewrite a program using raw pointers to use references where possible, justifying each remaining pointer and checking for null

schedule.title: Data structures by hand and memory safety
schedule.exercise: Compare in a short table a linked list and a dynamic array for insertion, lookup and memory use.

tasks.title: Insert, delete and reverse nodes of a singly linked list in the visualiser, watching pointers change at each step
Implement a linked list and a dynamic array with unique_ptr ownership so no manual delete is needed, and test with 100 inserts
Find and fix four planted memory errors, a leak, a double free, an overflow and a use-after-free, using sanitizer-style reports

schedule.title: Classes, constructors and operators
schedule.exercise: Design on paper a Fraction class with its members and describe which operators it should overload and why.

tasks.title: Write a Student class with private data, public methods and an interface and implementation split, and exercise it in main
Write a class that owns a dynamic array with a destructor, copy constructor and copy assignment, and show the rule of three prevents a double free
Build a Money or Fraction class with overloaded arithmetic, comparison and stream operators, and test all operators with 15 cases

schedule.title: Static members, inheritance and polymorphism
schedule.exercise: Draw a class hierarchy for shapes with a virtual area function and describe what a base class pointer does at run time.

tasks.title: Add a static counter of objects and a const member function to a class, and show the count after creating and destroying five objects
Build an abstract Shape base class with Circle and Rectangle subclasses and compute total area through a vector of base pointers
Trace virtual dispatch through a vtable in the visualiser, then find and fix a missing virtual destructor that leaks memory

schedule.title: Templates and the capstone project
schedule.exercise: Write a short design document for a library or inventory system, listing its classes, their responsibilities and the file format.

tasks.title: Write a class template for a simple Stack and use it with ints and strings, then replace it with std::vector and compare
Create the classes of a library system with add, search and borrow functions, and test them with a script of 20 operations
Complete a bank, library or inventory system with file persistence, templates, smart pointers and error handling, and show it survives a restart
